accuracy.evidence: Every fact recomputed: 6 × 10 = 60, 5 × 6 = 30 (half of 60), 2 × 7 = 14 = 7 + 7, the 3/5/15 family (3 × 5, 5 × 3, 15 ÷ 5 = 3, 15 ÷ 3 = 5), 20 ÷ 2 = 10, 50 ÷ 10 = 5, 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Parameterised items checked at range corners by the items gate. NC Year 2 multiplication and division wording (recall and use facts for the 2, 5 and 10 tables; multiplication in any order, division not) checked against the DfE programme of study.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented KS1 errors (NCETM Year 2 guidance and common misconception lists): adding instead of multiplying (5 × 4 = 9, tag add), writing digits side by side for ×10 (610, 108, tag join), subtracting or multiplying when dividing (30 ÷ 5 = 25 or 150, tags sub and mul), 5s not seen as half of 10s (55, 65, tag half), and treating division as commutative (4 ÷ 40 = 10 in m7, tag fam).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagttfam is about recall and derived facts: 10p coins dropped into a tray with the live sentence n × 10, six tens sticks each tapped to cut in half (5s = half of 10s), bikes parked to show 2 × 7 as a double, number cards dragged into the four sentences of one fact family triangle, and a covered triangle corner answered from three tiles. flagskip hops a track and flagcommul flips arrays; neither builds fact families or division facts.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers each link before the text names it: the coin count only reads 60 after six coins and all products end in 0; the green half of each stick shows 30 left of 60; the 2 + 2 + … line under the bikes turns into 14; a wrong card in a division sentence says 'how many 5s make 15?'; a wrong corner tile names the slip (that is 20 − 2, or 20 × 2) before the right fact is shown.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions each with a tempting wrong option: 6 × 10 as 16 or 610, 5 × 6 as 55 (take away 5) or 65, 2 × 7 as 7 + 2, 15 ÷ 5 as 10 or 75, and 20 ÷ 2 as 18 or 40. The task line then reveals 'You predicted …; now you know why it’s …' from the kit.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions (5 × 4, 10 × 8, 30 ÷ 5, 2 × 9, 5 × 7 from 10 × 7, a fact family, 16 ÷ 2), each wrong option tagged: add (added the numbers), join (digits side by side), sub (took away), mul (multiplied when dividing), half (5s are half the 10s), fam (division order in a family). Each tag has its own message naming the slip.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation FK grade about −0.8 and adult 8.9 (family targets 5.0 and 10.0, checked with learn/readability.py). Kid sentences are short and concrete (groups, coins, bikes, hands); curriculum words multiplication fact, division fact, fact family, multiple and commutative are used and explained.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what a times fact is; 10s end in 0; 5s are half the 10s and 2s are doubles; one fact gives four, with the 15 ÷ 5 slip. Adult: Year 2 statements, the three links and the inverse, six named mistakes, then what the lab does. No filler pattern matched and the overlap gate passed against every other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light at every step: coins wrap to rows of five inside 358 px, six sticks fit with 12 px gaps, bikes wrap four per row, the triangle sits above the four fact lines and the cards, and the cover tiles fit three across. Canvas labels are 14–30 px, feedback wraps to at most three lines below the drawing, and the young class makes the buttons 56 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin ('Add a 10p coin', 'Cut the next ten in half', 'Park a bike', one button per number card labelled with the sentence it fills, one per cover tile). The canvas aria-label and the live region carry each message. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
